The EU AI Act addresses data protection by complementing existing regulatory frameworks, particularly the GDPR, which remains applicable when AI systems process personal data. This includes requirements related to automated decisions with significant effects, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, and privacy by design. Companies must ensure that their contracts specify roles and responsibilities, including data processing agreements, and that they comply with data protection requirements when using external AI services.

Regarding transparency obligations, the AI Act mandates that users must be able to recognize when they are interacting with an AI system. For high-risk AI systems, there are specific requirements for risk assessment, documentation, and transparency regarding the AI's operation and potential risks. Providers must disclose foreseeable risks to health, safety, or fundamental rights, and ensure that users have access to clear and comprehensible system documentation to facilitate understanding and contestation of AI outputs. This integration of transparency into the design of AI systems aims to protect fundamental rights and ensure accountability.
